fullPassage:
Over time, certain biological and behavioral features of humans stop serving a purpose. Instead of disappearing completely, they remain intact but have no function. This is what happened with the grasp reflex. If you place an object in an infant's hand, he or she will automatically grab it. This reflex was helpful for our distant ancestors, whose babies had to hold tightly to their mothers' fur. But the grasp reflex is of little use to human babies now, as they don't have to cling for survival. Another unnecessary feature we inherited from our ancestors is goose bumps. Goose bumps occur when we are cold or frightened and the hairs on our body stand straight up. Today, they are anything but useful. But they kept our hairy ancestors warm because the erect hairs prevented body heat from escaping. They also made our ancestors appear larger, helping them scare away predators.

The iris is a muscle found in the eye. It can control the amount of light that enters the eye by opening and closing the pupil. Each of a person's two irises has a pattern of textures which is different from that of the other, as these patterns are not genetic. DNA decides the color and structure of the iris, but the patterns are formed randomly while the baby is still developing in the womb. As the baby opens and closes its eyes, the tissue of the iris moves and folds, creating patterns. Like fingerprints, iris patterns are unique and rarely change over time, so they are now often used for identification.

Dear Staff and Supporters, Our plan to move our bird exhibits to a larger space was intended to enhance the quality of the birds' lives. However, we have decided that our planned move is not necessarily a good idea at the present time. In-depth discussions with experts have led us to believe that the move could produce dangerous levels of stress as well as potential health risks for the birds. Not every member of the zoo's board of directors agreed, but we have decided to cancel the move. While this is not quite the outcome we had hoped for, we will continue to seek out other ways of improving our bird exhibits. Thank you for your understanding and support. Sincerely, Zoo Manager

In the 15th century, some Europeans used a strange medicine to stay healthy. It was called "mumia," and it was made from ground-up mummies. People ate it or rubbed it into injuries. They believed it could be used to treat coughs and headaches. However, mumia was not always embraced by the medical community. Additionally, not all patients were willing to try it. Despite this, there was still a high demand for mumia in Europe. Some people dug up Egyptian graves to steal the mummies. Others attempted to turn the bodies of people who had recently died into mummies. Modern people would view this practice as a kind of cannibalism. Medieval Europeans, however, considered it an unusual type of medicine. Fortunately, as medical knowledge advanced, doctors eventually stopped prescribing mumia.

A parasocial relationship occurs when an individual invests emotional energy, interest, and time in someone who is unaware of their existence. Commonly seen with fans of celebrities, these one-sided relationships allow individuals to attach themselves without the fear of disapproval or rejection. Even if there is no chance of a real interaction, studies indicate that these chosen relationships offer companionship and emotional support, especially during difficult times. These relationships are by no means meaningless because they have been shown to play a role in shaping an individual's personal identity. There is no doubt at all that parasocial relationships can hold significant value in enriching one's life.

Before the 16th century, there were no sizing systems for clothing whatsoever. Then, in 1589, one of the first written works related to the tailoring of clothes was published. This may have represented the beginnings of modern measurement standards. At the start of the 19th century, however, clothes were still being measured individually. It was a series of wars that finally led to the establishment of universal sizing, due to a sudden increase in the demand for military uniforms. By the end of the century, men's clothing was being sold in standardized sizes that didn't require any additional measurements. Women's clothing, however, took longer to change, as it was generally much more close-fitting. It wasn't until the early 20th century that ready-to-wear women's clothing became popular.

questions.passage: Over time, certain biological and behavioral features of humans stop serving a purpose. Instead of disappearing completely, they remain intact but have no function. This reflex was helpful for our distant ancestors, whose babies had to hold tightly to their mothers' fur. But the grasp reflex is of little use to human babies now, as they don't have to cling for survival. Another unnecessary feature we inherited from our ancestors is goose bumps. Goose bumps occur when we are cold or frightened and the hairs on our body stand straight up. Today, they are anything but useful. But they kept our hairy ancestors (B)[cold / warm] because the erect hairs (C)[prevented / allowed] body heat from escaping. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) automatically=자동으로 / reluctantly=마지못해 (B) warm=따뜻한 / cold=추운 (C) prevented=막았다 / allowed=허용했다
det.analysis:
① reluctantly—cold—allowed: (A) 아기는 물건을 '자동으로'(automatically) 쥠 (B) 조상을 '따뜻하게'(warm) 함
② automatically—cold—prevented: (B) 소름은 조상을 '따뜻하게'(warm) 유지
③ automatically—warm—prevented: 물건을 '자동으로' 쥠, 조상을 '따뜻하게' 함, 열 손실을 '막음'(prevented) ←정답
④ reluctantly—warm—allowed: (A)(C) 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 물건을 '자동으로'(automatically) 쥠 → 조상을 '따뜻하게'(warm) → 열이 빠져나가는 걸 '막음'(prevented)

As the baby opens and closes its eyes, the tissue of the iris moves and folds, creating patterns. Like fingerprints, iris patterns are unique and rarely change over time, so they are now often used for (C)[identification / decoration].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) decides=결정하다 / hides=숨기다 (B) developing=발달하는 / disappearing=사라지는 (C) identification=신원 확인 / decoration=장식
det.analysis:
① decides—developing—identification: DNA가 색·구조를 결정 + 아기가 자궁에서 발달하는 동안 + 신원 확인에 사용 ←정답
② hides—developing—identification: (A) DNA가 색·구조를 '숨기는' 게 아니라 결정(decides)함
③ decides—disappearing—decoration: (B)(C) 아기는 사라지는 게 아니라 발달(developing)하고, 무늬는 장식이 아니라 신원 확인(identification)에 쓰임
④ hides—disappearing—decoration: (A)(B)(C) 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: DNA가 색·구조를 decides(결정), 아기가 developing(발달), 무늬가 identification(신원 확인)에 쓰임

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) intact=온전한 / broken=손상된 (B) helpful=도움이 되는 / useless=쓸모없는 (C) unnecessary=불필요한 / essential=필수적인
det.analysis:
① intact—helpful—unnecessary: 특성이 사라지지 않고 '온전히' 남지만, 파악 반사는 조상에게 '도움이 되었고', 소름은 물려받은 '불필요한' 특성 ←정답
② broken—helpful—essential: (A) 사라지지 않고 온전히(intact) 남음 (C) 기능 없는 불필요한(unnecessary) 특성
③ intact—useless—unnecessary: (B) 파악 반사는 조상에게 도움이 됨(helpful)
④ broken—useless—essential: (A)(B)(C) 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 특성이 '온전히'(intact) 남음 → 파악 반사는 조상에게 '도움'(helpful) → 소름은 '불필요한'(unnecessary) 특성

questions.passage: The iris is a muscle found in the eye. It can (A)[block / control] the amount of light that enters the eye by opening and closing the pupil. Each of a person's two irises has a pattern of textures which is (B)[different / identical] from that of the other, as these patterns are not genetic. DNA decides the color and structure of the iris, but the patterns are formed randomly while the baby is still developing in the womb. As the baby opens and closes its eyes, the tissue of the iris moves and folds, creating patterns. Like fingerprints, iris patterns are (C)[unique / common] and rarely change over time, so they are now often used for identification.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) control=조절하다 / block=막다 (B) different=다른 / identical=동일한 (C) unique=고유한 / common=흔한
det.analysis:
① block—different—common: (A) 홍채는 빛의 양을 '막는' 게 아니라 동공을 여닫아 조절(control)함, (C) 홍채 무늬는 흔한 게 아니라 고유(unique)함
② control—different—unique: 빛의 양을 조절 + 다른 홍채와 다름 + 고유한 무늬 ←정답
③ control—identical—unique: (B) 두 홍채 무늬는 동일한 게 아니라 서로 다름(different)
④ block—identical—common: (A)(B)(C) 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 홍채는 빛의 양을 control(조절), 두 홍채는 서로 different(다름), 무늬는 unique(고유)

questions.passage: Dear Staff and Supporters, Our plan to move our bird exhibits to a larger space was intended to ①<u>enhance</u> the quality of the birds' lives. However, we have decided that our planned move is not necessarily a good idea at the present time. Not every member of the zoo's board of directors agreed, but we have decided to ③<u>continue</u> the move. While this is not quite the outcome we had hoped for, we will continue to seek out other ways of ④<u>improving</u> our bird exhibits. Thank you for your understanding and support. Sincerely, Zoo Manager
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① enhance=향상시키다 ② produce=야기하다 ③ cancel→continue (부적절) ④ improving=개선하는
det.analysis:
① enhance: 삶의 질을 향상시키려 이동을 계획함 — 적절
② produce: 이동이 위험한 수준의 스트레스를 야기할 수 있음 — 적절
③ continue: 이동을 '계속하기로(continue)' 결정했다? 글 전체는 이동을 '취소(cancel)'한다는 내용이라 반대 ←정답
④ improving: 전시를 개선하는 다른 방법을 찾겠다 — 적절
det.tip: 글의 핵심은 이동을 cancel(취소)하는 것. continue(계속)는 정반대

questions.passage: In the 15th century, some Europeans used a strange medicine to stay healthy. It was called "mumia," and it was made from ground-up mummies. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: price=가격 / fear=두려움 / refusal=거부 / demand=수요
det.analysis:
① price: 높은 '가격'? 다음에 for가 오는 흐름과 어색
② fear: 높은 '두려움'? 무관
③ refusal: 높은 '거부'? 문맥 반대
④ demand: 거부에도 불구하고 여전히 높은 '수요(demand)'가 있었음 ←정답
det.tip: still a high ___ for mumia = 여전히 높은 수요(demand)

questions.passage: A parasocial relationship occurs when an individual invests emotional energy, interest, and time in someone who is unaware of their existence. Commonly seen with fans of celebrities, these one-sided relationships allow individuals to (A)[attach / detach] themselves without the fear of disapproval or rejection. Even if there is no chance of a real interaction, studies (B)[deny / indicate] that these chosen relationships offer companionship and emotional support, especially during difficult times. These relationships are by no means meaningless because they have been shown to play a role in shaping an individual's personal identity. There is no doubt at all that parasocial relationships can hold (C)[trivial / significant] value in enriching one's life.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) attach=애착을 갖다 / detach=떼어 놓다 (B) indicate=보여주다 / deny=부인하다 (C) significant=상당한 / trivial=사소한
det.analysis:
(A) 개인이 스스로를 '애착시킬(attach)' 수 있게 해 준다는 흐름 — detach(떼어 놓다)는 반대
(B) 연구가 이런 관계의 이점을 '보여준다(indicate)' — deny(부인하다)는 반대
(C) 준사회적 관계가 '상당한(significant)' 가치를 지닐 수 있다 — trivial(사소한)은 반대
① attach — indicate — significant ←정답
det.tip: 애착(attach) → 연구가 보여줌(indicate) → 상당한 가치(significant)

questions.passage: Before the 16th century, there were no sizing systems for clothing whatsoever. Then, in 1589, one of the first written works related to the tailoring of clothes was published. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) universal=보편적인 / limited=제한된 (B) standardized=표준화된 / customized=맞춤형의 (C) additional=추가적인 / basic=기본적인
det.analysis:
① limited—standardized—additional: (A) 전쟁이 '보편적' 치수 체계를 확립시킴, '제한된'은 부적절
② universal—customized—basic: (B)(C) 문맥과 반대
③ universal—standardized—additional: 보편적 치수 확립 + 표준화된 사이즈로 판매 + 추가 측정이 불필요 ←정답
④ limited—customized—additional: (A)(B) 문맥과 반대
det.tip: universal(보편적) 치수 → standardized(표준화된) 사이즈 → additional(추가) 측정 불필요
